name: Ms. Qurrat Ul Ain Rehman
title: Founding Partner
description: Ms. Qurrat Ul Ain Rehman is a seasoned legal professional with over 11 years of advocacy and litigation experience, currently serving as Founding and Senior Partner at R & H Law Associates and Consultants. Her practice focuses on constitutional law, property law, family law, service law, corporate law, and immigration law, where she has successfully represented individuals and organizations in complex legal matters across diverse areas of law.

An LLM graduate in International Human Rights Law from Brunel University London, she brings a comparative and cross-jurisdictional perspective to her profile. Her advanced training includes International Human Rights Systems, Humanitarian Law, AI and Ethics, Islamic law, and Comparative Criminal Justice, allowing her to approach cases with both depth and innovation. Her academic and scholarly research on various topics of human rights law is published in reputable research journals.

Her advocacy work is enriched by extensive research and litigation experience, developed through her diverse roles at the Citizen Advice Bureau (UK), Legal Aid Bureau (Pakistan), and Ministry of Law & Justice, Pakistan. In these roles, she has worked on pro bono litigation, drafted legal instruments, and contributed to law reform initiatives aimed at strengthening access to justice and protecting vulnerable populations. She has also worked as a Senior Editor at JURIST Legal News & Commentary (US), and served as a member of the IUCN World Commission on Environmental Law. In both these roles she has published and actively engaged in discussions on contemporary human rights and envionmental law issues.

Known for her client-centred advocacy, strategic litigation skills, and commitment to social justice, Ms. Rehman stands out as a legal professional who bridges practice, policy, and research with integrity and impact.

name: Ms. Hareem Hilal
title: Founding Partner
description: Ms. Hareem Hilal is a legally trained academic and legal consultant with a robust background in civil law and constitutional law, backed by over seven years of diverse professional experience across academia, government, and legal practice.

In her legal consultancy role, Ms. Hilal provides expert opinion and analysis on a broad range of regulatory, commercial, and administrative legal matters. She regularly advises on the drafting and review of legal instruments, including contracts, wills, and powers of attorney, ensuring compliance with statutory frameworks. Her consultation spans across various fields of law, including Company Law, Competition Law, Arbitration, Succession Law, Tax Law, and Immigration Law. In her litigation practice, she has drafted and pleaded civil cases before the district courts, handling matters related to specific relief, contractual disputes, and property rights, combining technical precision with strategic legal advocacy. As a licensed Advocate of the High Court, she provides legal insight and strategic counsel to policy circles, development sectors, and legal institutions.

She has also worked in key public sector roles, notably as a Planning Officer at the Planning & Development Department, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where she supported the implementation of the Merged Areas Governance Project, conducted policy appraisals, and coordinated planning functions in development sectors. Moreover, she has served as a District Youth Officer, Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where she contributed to youth empowerment through district-level initiatives aligned with government youth policy objectives.

Academically, she holds an LLM in Public International Law from the University of Oslo (Norway), with a research specialization in human rights and climate change. Her scholarly work has been published in both national and international journals, covering themes like regional human rights protection, sexual trafficking, and climate law comparisons between the EU and the US. She has served as a Board Member of the UN Student Association Oslo (Norway), and is a Member of the IUCN World Commission on Environmental Law (2021 - 2025).

With a well-rounded mix of academic rigor, litigation practice, and legal consultancy, Ms. Hilal brings pragmatic, research-driven, and rights-conscious solutions to legal and policy challenges at both national and international levels.
